title: Design file storage and upload
summary: A file sync and sharing service: metadata in a database, bytes in object storage, presigned and resumable multipart uploads, content-hash dedupe and sync conflicts.

steps.title: Requirements and estimates
body: **The ask:** users upload files from phones and laptops, see them on every device, share them by link.
| Kind | Requirement |
| Functional | upload (large files too, over bad networks), download, list folders, share a link, sync changes to other devices |
| Non-functional | never lose or corrupt a file (durability first); uploads resume after a dropped connection; metadata changes visible on other devices within seconds |
| Out of scope | real-time co-editing of documents, virus scanning (mention it as a pipeline step) |
```text
users      10 M daily active
uploads    2 / user / day x 3 MB average = 60 TB / day of new bytes
bandwidth  60 TB / 86,400 s ≈ 690 MB/s ≈ 5.6 Gbit/s average, peaks 2-3x that
metadata   20 M new file rows / day x ~1 KB = 20 GB / day: small, but read constantly
Two very different data sets: **huge, write-once bytes** and **small, busy metadata**. They belong in different
stores.

steps.explain: Bytes to bits is x 8; a day is 86,400 seconds; Gbit is 10^9 bits. 60 TB a day is only 5.6 Gbit/s on average, but pushing it through your API servers would still need a fleet of them just for network cards.

steps.title: Bytes go straight to object storage
body: ```text
client --(1) POST /uploads {name, size, sha256}--> API --> metadata DB (file, version, status=pending)
<--(2) upload id + presigned part URLs -----
client --(3) PUT part 1..n directly ------------------------> object storage (bucket)
client --(4) POST /uploads/{id}/complete {part ETags} --> API --> complete multipart, status=ready
--> event --> sync service --> other devices
- A **presigned URL** is a link the API signs with its own credentials, valid for one object and a few minutes.
The client uploads directly; the API servers never carry the bytes.
- **Multipart upload** splits a big file into parts uploaded independently (in parallel, and retried one by
one). On Amazon S3, for example, parts are at least 5 MiB (except the last) and an upload has at most 10,000
parts; other object stores have similar rules.
- **Resumable:** after a dropped connection the client asks which parts the store already has and sends only
the rest.
- The **metadata DB** holds names, folders, versions, owners, sharing and the object key. It is what every
listing and every sync reads.

steps.prompt: Where does each piece of data live?
items: The folder tree and file names
Who a file is shared with
Each version's content hash and object key
Old versions' bytes kept for 30 days
steps.explain: Rule of thumb: anything you query, filter, join or update in place goes in the database; large immutable blobs go in object storage, addressed by a key the database stores.

prompt: **Symptom first.** Upload latency is terrible at peak. The API fleet dashboard:
```text
api servers         24 instances
CPU                 18% average
network out / in    9.4 Gbit/s in per instance (the NIC limit is 10)
upload handler      reads the request body and streams it to the bucket
What is the best fix?
options: Hand out presigned (multipart) URLs so clients upload straight to object storage; the API only handles metadata
Double the instance count: the CPU is fine, so they are cheap
Compress files on the API servers before storing them
Move the API servers into the same zone as the bucket
steps.explain: The servers are network-bound, not CPU-bound, because they proxy every byte. Doubling them doubles the bill for a job object storage does natively. Presigned uploads remove the bytes from the API path entirely.

steps.title: Dedupe and sync conflicts
body: - **Content-hash dedupe.** Split files into chunks (fixed size, or content-defined chunking so an insert near
the start does not shift every chunk) and name each chunk by its SHA-256. Upload only chunks the store does
not have. Keep a **reference count** per chunk; delete the bytes only when it reaches zero.
- **Privacy note:** global dedupe across users leaks information ("does anyone have this exact file?"). Many
services dedupe only within one account.
- **Sync conflicts.** Each file has a version number. A device uploads with "I edited version 7". If the server is
already at 8, the edit is a conflict: keep both ("report (conflicted copy).docx") rather than silently
overwrite someone's work. Last-writer-wins loses data.

steps.prompt: Put a resumable upload after a dropped connection in order.
lines: The client asks the API for the upload's state
The API lists the parts the object store already has
The client uploads only the missing parts to their presigned URLs
The client asks the API to complete the upload with every part's ETag
The API marks the version ready and the sync service notifies other devices

steps.title: Plan the parts
prompt: Write `long[] PartSizes(long fileSize, long partSize)`: the size of each part of a multipart upload, in order.
Every part is `partSize` except the last, which holds the remainder.
Throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when:
- `fileSize` is `0` or less;
- `partSize` is under 5 MiB (`5 * 1024 * 1024` bytes);
- the file would need more than 10,000 parts.
solution: if (partSize < 5 * MiB) throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(partSize), "parts are at least 5 MiB");
for (var i = 0; i < count; i++) parts[i] = Math.Min(partSize, fileSize - i * partSize);
hints: The part count is `(fileSize + partSize - 1) / partSize` (rounding up).
template: {{CODE}}
const long dojoMiB = 1024 * 1024;
Dojo.Eq("12 MiB in 5 MiB parts", new long[] { 5 * dojoMiB, 5 * dojoMiB, 2 * dojoMiB }, PartSizes(12 * dojoMiB, 5 * dojoMiB));
Dojo.Eq("an exact fit has no tiny last part", new long[] { 5 * dojoMiB, 5 * dojoMiB }, PartSizes(10 * dojoMiB, 5 * dojoMiB));
Dojo.Eq("a tiny file is one part", new long[] { 1 }, PartSizes(1, 5 * dojoMiB));
Dojo.Eq("50 GiB in 8 MiB parts", 6400, PartSizes(50 * 1024 * dojoMiB, 8 * dojoMiB).Length);
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("too many parts", () => PartSizes(10_001 * 5 * dojoMiB, 5 * dojoMiB));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("parts too small", () => PartSizes(100, dojoMiB));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("an empty file", () => PartSizes(0, 5 * dojoMiB));

steps.title: A deduplicating chunk store
prompt: Write a class `ChunkStore` that stores chunks by content hash with reference counts:
- `int Upload(IEnumerable<string> chunkHashes)`: one file's chunks. Each hash adds one reference. Return how many
chunks had to be **uploaded** (hashes the store did not have yet; a hash repeated inside the same file is
uploaded once).
- `int Stored`: how many distinct chunks are stored.
- `int RefCount(string hash)`: references to that chunk (`0` if unknown).
- `int Delete(IEnumerable<string> chunkHashes)`: one file is deleted: remove one reference per hash. A chunk whose
count reaches `0` is freed. Return how many chunks were freed. Deleting a hash that is not stored throws
`InvalidOperationException`.
solution: public int RefCount(string hash) => refs.TryGetValue(hash, out var n) ? n : 0;
if (!refs.TryGetValue(h, out var n)) throw new InvalidOperationException($"chunk {h} is not stored");
hints: A `Dictionary<string, int>` of hash -> reference count is the whole store.
On delete, a count of 1 means this was the last reference: remove the entry and count it as freed.
template: var dojoS = new ChunkStore();
Dojo.Eq("a file with a repeated chunk uploads it once", 2, dojoS.Upload(new[] { "a", "b", "a" }));
Dojo.Eq("a second file shares chunk b", 1, dojoS.Upload(new[] { "b", "c" }));
Dojo.Eq("three distinct chunks", 3, dojoS.Stored);
Dojo.Eq("b is referenced twice", 2, dojoS.RefCount("b"));
Dojo.Eq("a is referenced twice by one file", 2, dojoS.RefCount("a"));
Dojo.Eq("deleting the first file frees only a", 1, dojoS.Delete(new[] { "a", "b", "a" }));
Dojo.Eq("b and c remain", 2, dojoS.Stored);
Dojo.Eq("b has one reference left", 1, dojoS.RefCount("b"));
Dojo.Eq("unknown chunks have no references", 0, dojoS.RefCount("zzz"));
Dojo.Throws<InvalidOperationException>("deleting a chunk that is not stored", () => dojoS.Delete(new[] { "zzz" }));
{{CODE}}
